We can treat constraints as inequalities. The feasible region is polygon bounded by axes (n_A≥0, n_B≥0) and the two lines.

Find intersection of time and energy constraints:

Time line: 60 n_A + 40 n_B = 200 → divide 20: 3 n_A + 2 n_B = 10 → n_B = (10 - 3 n_A)/2.

Energy line: 180 n_A + 240 n_B = 800 → divide 60: 3 n_A + 4 n_B = 13.333... (800/60 = 13.3333). So n_B = (13.333... - 3 n_A)/4.

Find intersection solving both equalities:

Set n_B from time = n_B from energy:

(10 - 3 n_A)/2 = (13.333... - 3 n_A)/4

Multiply 4: 2*(10 - 3 n_A) = 13.333... - 3 n_A

=> 20 - 6 n_A = 13.333... - 3 n_A

=> 20 - 13.333... = 6 n_A - 3 n_A = 3 n_A

=> 6.6667 = 3 n_A → n_A = 2.2222... (2 2/9). n_A = 20/9 ≈ 2.222.

Plug into time line to get n_B: n_B = (10 - 3*(20/9))/2 = (10 - 60/9)/2 = (10 - 6.6667)/2 = 3.3333/2 = 1.6667. So n_B = 5/3 ≈ 1.6667.

Check constraints: both satisfied equality.

Now compute Q at this point: Q = 540 n_A + 600 n_B = 540*(20/9) + 600*(5/3) = (540*20)/9 + (600*5)/3 = (540/9=60) => 60*20 = 1200. For second: 600/3=200 => 200*5 = 1000. Total Q = 2200 kJ.

Thus maximum Q is 2200 kJ (since objective coefficients positive, optimum at intersection of constraints). So heat requirement 2160 is achievable.
